key_insight: PyRUA-DataFarm proposes using an LLM coding agent to take over parts of robot demonstration collection. Given a data request and one calibration episode, the agent builds a simulated task with an expert controller and a success checker.
problem_solved: Robot teleoperation consumes both operator and robot time, and collecting demonstrations for each new task often requires starting from scratch.
method: Provide the agent with a task-specific data request and one robot calibration episode from the target scene.
Have the agent write the simulated scene, an expert controller, and a success judge.
Use the simulator to supply exact actions; the provided abstract is truncated before explaining the video model's role.
impact: This approach could reduce repeated human teleoperation and make robot training data easier to generate across tasks. The provided excerpt does not establish cost savings or real-world performance.
visual_elements: Workflow: data request + calibration episode → coding agent → simulated task → demonstrations.
Three-module diagram showing the generated scene, expert controller, and success judge.
Side-by-side illustration of human teleoperation versus agent-driven simulation.
Robot-time and operator-time icons highlighting the collection costs the method targets.
paper_title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
paper_authors: Kewei Zhang, Juncheng Ma, Guodong Lv, Duomin Wang, Feixiang Ruan
